faq.a: Petals attract animal pollinators with colour, pattern and often scent. Many have lines or patches, some visible only in ultraviolet light, that guide bees to the nectar.
The stamen is the male part of a flower. Its anther makes pollen, which carries the male cells, and its filament holds the anther where visitors will brush against it.
The stigma is the sticky tip of the female part. It catches pollen grains, and if the pollen is from the right kind of plant, a pollen tube grows down to the ovary.
asks: What is the female part of a flower?

faq.a: After fertilisation, the ovules in the ovary become seeds and the ovary itself grows into a fruit. An apple, a tomato and a pea pod all grew from ovaries.
Sepals are the small, usually green, leaf-like parts under the petals. They wrap and protect the flower while it is still a bud.
asks: What is the green part under a flower?

facts: The stamen is made of the anther and filament; the carpel is made of the stigma, style and ovary.
A fruit develops from the ovary of a flower, and its seeds develop from the ovules.
Many flowers have ultraviolet patterns that bees can see but people cannot.

quiz.say: Which part of a flower becomes the fruit?
quiz.show: Which part of a flower becomes the fruit?
quiz.why: After fertilisation the ovary swells into a fruit with the seeds inside.
